scope: Connection-bound one-shot edit calls with immutable captured intent, worker-encoded metadata packet, queue admission publication and strict owned-response routing
evidenceNotes: Production GUI recompiles131 units after the opaque transport layout and request/call interfaces change. Native server bytes are unchanged. Reuse checks recompute actual compiler closures for101 service-linked objects including core members, with284 current source/header entries. Eight old client/auxiliary objects from the prior109-unit build are excluded. All current client/support/test consumers linked into the new native programs are newly built.

The first preparation helper fails its test-registration anchor assertion. The production build proceeds from its frozen complete production sources. Registration is corrected only inside the Tests branch after freezing; that branch is not used by the production command. Final audit proves the entire production sources/flags prefix identical and accounts for exactly the private object-root and test-registration deltas.

GUI-targeted-v1 preserves two real Werror misleading-indentation fixture diagnostics. GUI-targeted-v2 passes all five programs. Native-test-v1 passes identity checks but preserves a call-fixture Windows-version macro redefinition diagnostic after forced native headers. A conditional platform guard yields native-test-v2 success. Later test-owned client cleanup changes only the call fixture; final GUI-v4/native-final-v3 programs are separately frozen and executed.

Acceptance composes four unchanged GUI programs and the final call program, plus the unchanged native identity program/support objects and final native call program. Exact final sources and actual linked executables are bound. No unexecuted earlier snapshot copy is substituted for the final fixture.

Transport-v1 passes3426 receiver checks but invokes the existing lease fixture without its required arguments; that failed invocation remains raw. Transport-v2 supplies data directory, actual root-runtime server alias and compiler, passing2387 lease checks. Explicit acceptance counts only the two actually passed programs.

Twelve actual implementation mutants exit1 at fixture assertions. Cases remove peer/ID/method/token/input/scope binding, one-call claim, reply replay gates, UTF16 checking, cancellation/current flags, send peer checking or atomic send admission. Compile failures and crashes do not count.

The initial collector incorrectly required a disk file in the native fixture working directories. Native metadata/stdIO fixtures intentionally leave these directories file-empty. Its raw log and verified source archive are preserved unchanged; the corrected collection retains all GUI disk fixtures and the actual program/log evidence.

Positive routing uses an explicitly controlled stdio peer whose candidate contains intentionally invalid source proofs; routing success is not source admission. Actual IDE integration instead receives the unchanged real server standard -32601 error because no candidate RPC exists yet. No new native rename method or standard capability is claimed.

New identities add immutable storage and constructor atomic work. The bound path adds an admission CAS and immutable call metadata/encoding. Existing queue ownership and response roots are reused, but no whole-IDE latency/RSS, internal allocator failure matrix or zero-overhead claim is inferred.
limits: The candidate RPC, full proof/source/member/static-analysis/WorkspaceEdit decoder, background host/controller, negotiated capability and protocol cancellation still need implementation. Routing Candidate returns untrusted metadata only.

Source/physical identity, closed-target and owned-write publication policy, full owner Current gates, confirmation/recovery/startup replay, transactions and standard rename/applyEdit activation remain open.

Connection identities are process-lifetime metadata, not authentication; the caller must obtain peer identity and raw byte length from the actual transport/parser. Local ReplyCurrent is not the complete owner or disk fence.

Existing8MiB frame, context/scope and shared snapshot limits apply; encoder/DOM/allocator/temporary work and OS resources are additional. Failure before successful preparation may be retried, but a successfully claimed request never resets.

Other synchronous readers, latest engine/native frontend asset alignment, deep unprefixed xlp paths, analysis-configuration cache-count regression and full performance/resource/longevity qualification remain open.
C LSP remains disabled. No DAP/debug/runtime completion or Linux/sanitizer qualification in this stage.
